name: Longitude 131
insider_take: This isn't just a hotel – it's Australia's most exclusive desert sanctuary, where luxury tented pavilions offer unobstructed views of the world's largest monolith, Uluru.
whats_special: Longitude 131° features just 16 eco-luxe tented pavilions elevated on stilts, each with floor-to-ceiling windows facing Uluru. The property sits within UNESCO World Heritage-listed Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, making it one of the world's most exclusive wilderness lodges. The hotel's name references its exact geographical coordinates, emphasizing its unique position in Australia's Red Centre.
pro_tip: Book a pavilion on the northern end for the most dramatic sunrise views of Uluru. The "Field of Light" art installation by Bruce Munro illuminates the desert with 50,000 solar-powered lights after sunset – it's only a short walk from your tent.
dont_miss: The complimentary helicopter scenic flight over Uluru and Kata Tjuta (The Olgas), exclusive access to remote Aboriginal rock art sites with indigenous guides, and dining under the Southern Hemisphere's star-filled sky at the outdoor Table 131° restaurant. The nearby Mutitjulu Waterhole holds sacred Aboriginal significance and offers rare desert wildlife spotting opportunities.
pros: Unparalleled views of Uluru and Kata Tjuta from luxury tented pavilions
Exclusive access to private Uluru experiences and indigenous cultural activities
World-class dining featuring native Australian ingredients and wine pairings
Eco-luxury accommodations with sophisticated desert-inspired design
cons: Remote desert location requires planned transfers and limited nearby amenities
Premium pricing reflects ultra-luxury positioning and exclusive experience
